chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from one of our companions, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Why did Allah prohibit the wine?' He said: 'He prohibited it due to its action/effect, and whatever is inherited from its spoiling/decay.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah prohibit wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the principle of *'illa* (legal cause) by defining wine's prohibition through its intoxicating effects rather than its specific source. This establishes the basis for *khamr* being a genus (*jins*) in Shia jurisprudence, allowing for the extension of the prohibition to any substance that produces similar intoxication, regardless of its origin. The narration underscores that the legal ruling is tied to the functional outcome—loss of reason—rather than mere material composition.
